turns:
This is a subscription-service unit economics problem. You must show your work.

Assumptions:
- Monthly subscription price $29.00, payment processing fee 3.4%
- Variable server/ops cost per customer per month: $4.20
- Average subscription lifetime: 14 months
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC): $68.00 per new customer from paid ads

Questions:
1. Monthly contribution margin ($) and contribution margin rate (%)? (1 decimal place)
2. LTV? (contribution margin × lifetime)
3. LTV/CAC ratio? (1 decimal place)
4. CAC payback period in months? (1 decimal place)
5. Marketing wants to raise CAC to $85.00 — judge whether that is acceptable against a 3x LTV/CAC threshold.

rubric.name: Calculation accuracy
rubric.desc: All 5 answers correct (1: $23.81 / 82.1%, 2: $333.40, 3: 4.9, 4: 2.9 months, 5: acceptable at 3.9x)

rubric.name: Clarity of work
rubric.desc: Calculation logic is presented so it is easy to follow

rubric.name: Judgment quality
rubric.desc: Question 5 mentions headroom versus the threshold and the risks

en.reference:
1. Contribution margin = 29.00 - 29.00*0.034 (=0.986) - 4.20 = $23.814 ≈ $23.81, contribution margin rate = 23.814/29.00 = 82.1%
2. LTV = 23.814 * 14 = $333.396 ≈ $333.40
3. LTV/CAC = 333.396/68.00 = 4.9
4. Payback period = 68.00/23.814 = 2.9 months
5. Even at $85.00, 333.396/85.00 = 3.9x ≥ 3, so it is acceptable (bonus for noting sensitivity of the lifetime assumption)

버려야 할 것 1가지(선택과 집중) → 성공 지표.
'열심히 하자' 류의 공허한 말 금지, 모든 전략에 '왜 우리가 이길 수 있는지' 근거.

turns:
Write a response-strategy memo for the head of strategy at a collaboration software startup.

Situation:
- Us: all-in-one collaboration tool for US small and mid-sized businesses, 1,200 paying customers, ARPU $290/month
- Threat: a global collaboration suite giant just announced that next month it will cut its SMB-tier pricing by 40% and ship features aimed squarely at our segment
- Our strengths: fully integrated approval workflows and org directory built for regulated SMBs, 4-hour human support response, security accreditation for state and local government clients
- Our weaknesses: app performance (slow mobile loading), thin third-party integration ecosystem

Structure: situation assessment (size the real threat coldly) → 3 defensive strategies (immediate / 3-month / 1-year horizons) →
1 thing to stop doing (focus) → success metrics.
No empty 'let's work harder' talk; every strategy must state why we can win there.

rubric.name: Strategic thinking
rubric.desc: The threat assessment is clear-eyed and each strategy is grounded in evidence

rubric.name: Specificity
rubric.desc: Strategies concrete enough to execute (no empty platitudes)

rubric.name: Structure compliance
rubric.desc: Assessment → 3 strategies → thing to drop → metrics structure

rubric.name: Document quality
rubric.desc: Density and professional English worthy of a strategy memo
